 THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED:27.07.2017 PASSED IN MVC NO.4759/2015 ON THE FILE OF XXII ADDITIONAL SMALL CAUSES JUDGE & XX ACMM., & MEMBER MACT, BENGALURU, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.

The claimant, being dissatisfied with the compensation of Rs.1,04,400/- awarded by the Tribunal,
is in appeal.
2. The fact that the accident occurred and the further fact that the offending vehicle was insured is not in dispute.
3. The Tribunal, on an analysis of the medical evidence, has concluded that the claimant has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 7% to the whole body.
The Doctor who has been examined has assessed the disability of the claimant at 15% to the whole body.
In my view, the Tribunal could not have substituted its view in the light of the Doctor's evidence.
The disability to the whole body is taken as 15%.
4. The Tribunal has determined the monthly income, notionally at Rs.5,000/-.

Since there is no credible documentary evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority,
which, for the accident of the year 2015, would be Rs.9,000/-.

sentences.text: The Tribunal has considered the age of claimant as more than 60 years and hence, a multiplier of '7' would have to be applied.

Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.1,13,400/-
(Rs.9,000/- x 12 x '7' x 15%) towards 'loss of future income' .
6. As a consequence, the amount of Rs.10,000/- awarded by the Tribunal towards 'loss of income during the laid up period' would also stand enhanced to Rs.36,000/- (Rs.9,000/- X 4 months).

7. Having regard to the injuries suffered by the claimant and the fact that the claimant was hospitalised for 22 days, it would be appropriate to award Rs.50,000/- instead of Rs.30,000/-
towards 'pain and suffering'; Rs.50,000/- instead of Rs.20,000/- towards 'loss of amenities of life'
and Rs.30,000/- instead of Rs.15,000/- towards 'food and nourishment expenses, conveyance and attendant charges'.

8. Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the following sums are awarded as compensation:
 Sl. Particulars Award by Award by  No. Tribunal this Court  (Rs.) (Rs.)
1 . Pain
and suffering 30,000/- 50,000/-

2. Food and nourishment 15,000/- 30,000/-
 expenses, conveyance  and attendant charges  3. Loss of income during 10,000/- 36,000/-
 the period of  treatment  4. Loss of future 29,400/- 1,13,400/-
 earnings  5. Loss of amenities of 20,000/- 50,000/-
 life

9 . Thus, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.2,79,400/- as against Rs.1,04,400/-, along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
10. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

11. On such deposit, 50% is ordered to be invested in the name of claimant for a period of five years in any Nationalised or Scheduled Bank of her choice with liberty to withdraw the interest accrued thereon periodically.
After maturity, the Bank shall released the amount in favour of claimant without any further proceedings.
The remaining 50% amount shall be released in favour of claimant through account payee cheque after proper identification.
